To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the implantable defibrillators did not ensure reliable detection of ventricular tachycardia in patients using a new nonthorcotomy lead system.
the implantable defibrilator failed to detect ventricular fibrillation reliably in patients using a new lead system.

the amplitude of bipolar electrograms recorded from the nonthoracotomylad lead decreased after successful defibrillation and that failure to redetect ventricular fibrillation was documented at predischarge testing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the detection and localization of ventricular fibrillations in the human heart.
the development of a new implantable defibrillation lead system.
the detection of ventricle fibrillation in patients with a nonthoracotmy lead system and the failure of redetection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of sudden cardiac arrest persists despite implantable defibrillation therapy, and that the risk may be increased in patients using nonthoracotmy lead systems.
the risk of SCD in these patients is still high and that the use of the ICD should be restricted to patients with a high risk of SCD and a high risk of sudden arrhythmic death.
the nonthoracotomies leads are not suitable for implantable cardioverter‐defibrillator systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the implantable defibrillators are not always able to redetect ventricular fibrillation after shock delivery.
the nonthoracomy leads do not allow for reliable defibrillation and may be dangerous.
the nonthoracotomous leads are not reliable enough for defibrillation and the implantable defibrillators are not reliable enough in detecting fibrillations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amplitude of the electrograms recorded by the implanted lead system may be reduced by shock discharges, which may impair redetection of venticular fibrillation.
we need to be careful when implanting a new device.
we should not assume that a patient is safe from sudden death just because they have a defibrillator.
